resolution: User said they don't need InstantMesh color (will paint it themselves), which reframed the gap: the missing piece wasn't color, it was that the LIVE Studio editor couldn't import a .obj at all. Traced the live path (workbench/model/source.tsx -> studiokit -> StudioViewport -> studiokit/dialogs/ImportModelDialog) and found the req_1390 'lifted verbatim, no behavior change' decomposition had silently DROPPED the .obj branch: the extracted dialog only imported glbToEditMesh and always did glbToEditMesh(base64ToBytes(...)), so an InstantMesh .obj got decoded as base64 garbage and threw 'not a GLB file'. The frozen Studio.tsx breadcrumb still had the correct .obj-vs-.glb detection. Fix: restored the branch in the extracted dialog (objToEditMesh on text for .obj, glb path otherwise), re-imported readFile + objToEditMesh, and updated the dialog title/description + StudioViewport import-button tooltip to say 'GLB / OBJ'. objToEditMesh imports geometry only with UVs unwrapped fresh -- exactly the import-then-paint-myself flow. Verified: tools/tsc-check hmsc-int bundles clean (exit 0); importMesh.test.ts runs 6/6 PASS including the OBJ-quad parse case. Committed f3198147f (2 files: ImportModelDialog.tsx, StudioViewport.tsx).
